You are a fix worker on the OBE podcast repo. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast - edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit, branch, or push; leave changes uncommitted. No skills/MCP/network. PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1.

CONTEXT (live proof-run evidence, episode 2026-06-10-fred-cho): this machine's ffmpeg has NO libx264, so h264_encoder() (server/pipeline/video_assembly.py:41) returns libopenh264. No encode site sets a keyframe interval, and libopenh264 with no -g produces essentially a single IDR frame: the real 2919.6s composite.mp4 was ffprobe-verified to contain EXACTLY ONE keyframe (t=0). Consequence: every input-seek decode (ffmpeg -ss 2548.5 -i composite.mp4) must decode from t=0; a 6s segment render was measured at 131.8s wall, blowing angle_render's 120s segment timeout (angle_render.py:630 timeout_s = max(120, dur*4+60)), so the publishable render fails every attempt and the job parks review-required.

TASK: make every H.264 intermediate this pipeline encodes seekable by giving it an explicit keyframe interval.

OWNERSHIP: you own ONLY: server/pipeline/video_assembly.py, server/pipeline/angle_render.py, tests/test_video_assembly.py, tests/test_angle_render.py. Never modify anything else.

BUILD:
1. In server/pipeline/video_assembly.py add ONE shared helper next to h264_encoder(), e.g. def h264_encode_args(gop=60) -> list[str]: returns ['-c:v', h264_encoder()] plus ['-preset','veryfast'] only when the encoder is libx264, plus ['-g', str(gop)] always (60 frames at fps=30 = one keyframe every 2s; -g maps to libopenh264 uiIntraPeriod and to x264/nvenc GOP size, so it is safe for every encoder h264_encoder() or the PODCAST_H264_ENCODER override can return).
2. Adopt the helper at EVERY ffmpeg command in video_assembly.py that currently does '-c:v', encoder (9 sites: composite build, camera normalize, keep-timeline/apply, segment extracts, bumpers, etc.) and in angle_render.py _video_output_args() (line 259) which feeds both segment renders and seam bridges. Do not change any other flag at those sites (bitrate, pix_fmt, -reinit_filter, filters all stay).
3. Cache invalidation: in composite_side_by_side() the recipe dict currently says "recipe": "composite_side_by_side_v4" and records "encoder". Bump to composite_side_by_side_v5 AND record the full encode args list in the recipe (e.g. "encode_args": [...]) so the existing single-keyframe cached composite.mp4 is treated stale and rebuilt on the next run. If any other _composite_input_hash recipe covers an encode this change touches, record the args there too.
4. No behavior changes beyond the encode args + recipe bump. Do NOT touch the 120s timeout formula - with seekable input the seek cost disappears and the existing formula is correct.

TESTS (add to the owned test files):
(a) unit: h264_encode_args() contains '-g','60' and '-c:v'; _video_output_args() contains '-g','60'.
(b) executed keyframe-density proof: encode ~24s of lavfi testsrc2 (1280x720, 30fps, -t 24) through the new shared args (build the ffmpeg cmd from h264_encode_args()), then ffprobe -show_entries packet=flags and assert at least 8 keyframes (24s / 2s GOP = 12 expected; assert >=8 for slack). Skip cleanly if ffmpeg/ffprobe are unavailable.
(c) recipe: composite recipe dict includes the encode args and the v5 tag (assert via the recipe passed to _composite_input_hash, monkeypatch or refactor-safe inspection).
(d) ALL existing tests in the four owned test files stay green; if any asserted the old exact arg lists, update them and list which in the summary.

HOW TO RUN: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_video_assembly.py tests/test_video_assembly_bumpers.py tests/test_angle_render.py -q -p no:cacheprovider

OUTPUT CONTRACT: uncommitted changes + ./fix-summary.md ('# Fix Summary','## Summary','## Files Changed','## Verification','## Assumptions', <600 words).
